question: Which group of vitamins is most easily lost during prolonged soaking in water?
explanation: Vitamins such as C and B-complex dissolve readily in water and leach out when foods are soaked or boiled excessively. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T008#GNS227_U3_T008_h1)

question: Why is careful food preparation considered a critical healthcare intervention?

options.A: It shortens the hospital stay of surgical patients
options.B: It directly influences patient recovery and nutritional status
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for vitamin supplements
options.D: It reduces the financial cost of hospital catering services

explanation: Proper preparation ensures that essential nutrients are preserved and delivered to patients, supporting their healing process. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T008#GNS227_U3_T008_h1)

question: What is the primary purpose of sanitizing kitchen surfaces and cutting boards?

options.A: Accelerating the cooking time of protein foods
options.B: Enhancing the visual appearance of cooking utensils
options.C: Removing unpleasant odors from wooden surfaces

explanation: Sanitization eliminates harmful microorganisms from surfaces, stopping them from transferring to ready-to-eat foods. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T008#GNS227_U3_T008_h2)

question: Which practice is most effective for stopping the initial transmission of pathogens from a food handler to ingredients?

options.A: Rinsing hands in cold water without using any soap
options.B: Thorough handwashing with soap and running water
options.C: Applying perfumed hand lotion before touching food
options.D: Wearing thick rubber gloves throughout the entire day

explanation: Rigorous hand hygiene physically removes transient bacteria and viruses from the skin before food contact occurs. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T008#GNS227_U3_T008_h2)

question: What is the primary benefit of cutting vegetables into uniform sizes?

options.A: Preventing the loss of fat-soluble vitamins
options.B: Ensuring even cooking times across all pieces
options.C: Making the vegetables taste significantly sweeter
options.D: Eliminating the need for washing the produce

explanation: Uniform pieces heat at the same rate, preventing undercooked centers or burnt exterior edges. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T008#GNS227_U3_T008_h3)

question: Why are precise knife skills particularly important when preparing meals for patients with swallowing difficulties?

options.A: They reduce the amount of time needed to boil root vegetables
options.B: They prevent large, hazardous chunks from remaining in soft or pureed diets
options.C: They ensure that all vitamins remain fully locked inside the cell walls
options.D: They make the food look more appealing to patients with poor appetite

explanation: Consistent processing avoids accidental choking hazards by ensuring the texture is completely smooth or uniformly small. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T008#GNS227_U3_T008_h3)

question: Which of the following is an example of a moist-heat cooking method?
explanation: Steaming uses water vapor as the primary medium to transfer heat to the food item. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T008#GNS227_U3_T008_h4)

question: A patient requires a diet that minimizes the loss of water-soluble vitamins while avoiding added cooking fats. Which method is most appropriate?

options.A: Grilling over an open charcoal fire
options.C: Boiling in a large pot of water

explanation: Steaming keeps vegetables out of direct contact with boiling water, reducing vitamin leaching while requiring no added fat. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T008#GNS227_U3_T008_h4)

question: What is a major positive effect of cooking food besides improving flavor?

options.B: Permanently locking in all water-soluble vitamins
options.C: Doubling the concentration of mineral elements
options.D: Preventing the oxidation of dietary fats

explanation: Heat kills harmful microorganisms and breaks down complex molecules, making absorption easier for the body. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T008#GNS227_U3_T008_h5)

question: How can a nurse advise a caregiver to recover nutrients that leach into water during boiling?

options.A: Use the nutrient-rich cooking liquid as a base for soups or stews
options.B: Filter the water through a cloth to trap dissolved minerals
options.C: Add chemical preservatives to the leftover water before storage
options.D: Pour cold water over the cooked food immediately after boiling

explanation: Reincorporating the cooking liquid ensures that leached vitamins and minerals are consumed rather than discarded. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T008#GNS227_U3_T008_h5)

question: Where should raw meat be stored in a refrigerator to prevent cross-contamination?
explanation: Storing raw meat at the bottom ensures that any accidental fluid drips cannot contaminate other foods stored below. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T008#GNS227_U3_T008_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a safe practice for preventing foodborne illness in a kitchen?

options.A: Using the same unwashed cutting board for raw meat and fresh salad
options.B: Washing hands thoroughly after handling raw poultry and eggs
options.C: Storing ready-to-eat meals above raw ingredients in the fridge
options.D: Keeping hot cooked foods steaming hot until they are served

explanation: Using the same unwashed board transfers raw meat pathogens directly onto food that will not be cooked again, causing illness. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T008#GNS227_U3_T008_h6)

question: What is the primary culinary adjustment made when preparing food for a patient on a low-sodium diet?

options.A: Boiling all vegetables for at least two hours
options.B: Restricting salt and using herbs or spices for flavor
options.C: Increasing the amount of baking soda used in baking
options.D: Eliminating all liquids from the cooking process entirely

explanation: Sodium is restricted to manage blood pressure, while herbs and spices compensate for the reduction in saltiness. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T008#GNS227_U3_T008_h7)

question: A patient with chronic kidney disease needs dietary preparation that reduces potassium content in root vegetables. Which technique is most effective?

options.A: Dry roasting the vegetables directly over an open flame
options.B: Frying the slices quickly in high-temperature vegetable oil
options.C: Freezing the raw vegetables for several days before cooking
options.D: Leaching by cutting, soaking, and boiling in fresh water

explanation: Leaching draws water-soluble potassium out of root vegetables, helping renal patients stay within safe electrolyte limits. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T008#GNS227_U3_T008_h7)
